about: English meaning written for this library (en-scriptures): one per mantra, from the word meanings and the traditional understanding (Sāyaṇa, Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara as commonly summarised); not copied from any source.

m.namakam.purva.guru: Salutations to the revered Gurus. Hariḥ Om.
m.namakam.purva.ganapati: We invoke you, Gaṇapati, lord of the hosts — seer among seers, of the highest renown, eldest king of sacred prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati. Hear us, and come with your protection to take your seat here.
m.namakam.purva.samhita: The Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda: the fourth kāṇḍa (the Vaiśvadeva), its fifth prapāṭhaka.
m.namakam.purva.rudraya: Om, salutations to the blessed Lord Rudra.
m.namakam.a01.m01: O Rudra, salutations to your wrath and to your arrow; salutations to your bow and to both your arms.
m.namakam.a01.m02: May your arrow become most gracious and your bow gracious; your quiver too is gracious — with it, O Rudra, make us happy.
m.namakam.a01.m03: O Rudra, with that auspicious form of yours which is not fearsome and shows only good — with that most peaceful form, O Giriśanta, look upon us.
m.namakam.a01.m04: O Giriśanta, the arrow you hold in your hand to shoot — make it gracious, O guardian of the mountain; do not harm man or any living being.
m.namakam.a01.m05: O dweller on the mountain, we approach you with gracious words, so that our whole world — people and cattle — may be free of disease and of good cheer.
m.namakam.a01.m06: The foremost advocate, the divine physician, has spoken for us. Crushing all serpents, drive away all evil spirits.
m.namakam.a01.m07: He who is copper-red, then crimson, then golden-brown — the most auspicious Sun; and the thousands of Rudras who surround him in every direction — we pray that their anger be turned away.
m.namakam.a01.m08: He who moves across the sky, blue-throated and red — the cowherds have seen him, the women carrying water have seen him, and all beings; may he, being seen, make us happy.
m.namakam.a01.m09: Salutations to the blue-throated, thousand-eyed Rudra who showers blessings; and to his attendants also I offer salutations.
m.namakam.a01.m10: O Lord, release the string from both ends of your bow, and cast away the arrows in your hand.
m.namakam.a01.m11: O thousand-eyed one with a hundred quivers, unstringing your bow and blunting the points of your arrows, be gracious and kind to us.
m.namakam.a01.m12: May the bow of the matted-haired one be unstrung and his quiver empty of arrows; may his arrows lose their power and his sheath be empty.
m.namakam.a01.m13: O most bountiful one, with the weapon and the bow in your hand — now harmless — protect us on every side.
m.namakam.a01.m14: Salutations to your weapon, bold yet not aimed at us; salutations to both your arms and to your bow.
m.namakam.a01.m15: May the missile of your bow pass us by on every side; and place your quiver far away from us.
m.namakam.bhagavan.namaste: Salutations to you, O Lord — lord of the universe, the great god, three-eyed, destroyer of the three cities, the time of the three sacred fires, Rudra who is the fire of dissolution, blue-throated, conqueror of death, lord of all, ever-auspicious, Śaṅkara, the glorious great god.
m.namakam.a02.m01: Salutations to the golden-armed leader of armies; salutations to the lord of the directions.
m.namakam.a02.m02: Salutations to the trees with green leaves, his forms; to the lord of all beings (Paśupati), salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m03: Salutations to the radiant one, tawny like young grass; to the lord of the paths, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m04: Salutations to the brown-hued one who pierces the foe; to the lord of all food, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m05: Salutations to the green-haired one who wears the sacred thread; to the lord of the well-nourished, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m06: Salutations to him who is the weapon that ends worldly existence; to the lord of all that moves, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m07: Salutations to Rudra, whose bow is drawn to protect; to the lord of the fields, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m08: Salutations to the charioteer whom none can harm; to the lord of the forests, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m09: Salutations to the red one, the master builder; to the lord of the trees, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m10: Salutations to the counsellor and the merchant; to the lord of the thickets, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m11: Salutations to him who spread out the world and grants wealth to his devotees; to the lord of the healing herbs, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m12: Salutations to him of the loud battle-cry, who makes foes weep; to the lord of the foot-soldiers, salutations.
m.namakam.a02.m13: Salutations to him fully armoured, who runs to protect; to the lord of the strong, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m01: Salutations to the conqueror who pierces the foe; to the lord of the armies that strike from all sides, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m02: Salutations to the eminent one who bears the sword; to the lord of thieves, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m03: Salutations to him with sword and quiver; to the lord of robbers, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m04: Salutations to the deceiver and the arch-deceiver; to the lord of pilferers, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m05: Salutations to him who moves stealthily and roams about; to the lord of the forests, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m06: Salutations to those who carry spears and seek to strike; to the lord of plunderers, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m07: Salutations to the sword-bearers who roam at night; to the lord of cut-throats, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m08: Salutations to the turbaned one roaming the mountains; to the lord of land-grabbers, salutations.
m.namakam.a03.m09: Salutations to you who bear arrows and bows.
m.namakam.a03.m10: Salutations to you who string the bow and fit the arrow.
m.namakam.a03.m11: Salutations to you who draw the bow and release the arrow.
m.namakam.a03.m12: Salutations to you who shoot and who pierce the target.
m.namakam.a03.m13: Salutations to you who sit and who lie down.
m.namakam.a03.m14: Salutations to you who sleep and who wake.
m.namakam.a03.m15: Salutations to you who stand and who run.
m.namakam.a03.m16: Salutations to you who are the assemblies and the lords of assemblies.
m.namakam.a03.m17: Salutations to you who are the horses and the masters of horses.
m.namakam.a04.m01: Salutations to you, the powers who wound from every side and pierce in many ways.
m.namakam.a04.m02: Salutations to you, the noble hosts of goddesses and those that destroy.
m.namakam.a04.m03: Salutations to you, the covetous and the leaders of the covetous.
m.namakam.a04.m04: Salutations to you, the bands of men and the leaders of bands.
m.namakam.a04.m05: Salutations to you, the hosts (Śiva’s gaṇas) and the lords of hosts.
m.namakam.a04.m06: Salutations to you who are of strange form and of every form.
m.namakam.a04.m07: Salutations to you who are the great and the small.
m.namakam.a04.m08: Salutations to you who ride in chariots and who go without.
m.namakam.a04.m09: Salutations to you who are the chariots and the lords of chariots.
m.namakam.a04.m10: Salutations to you who are the armies and their commanders.
m.namakam.a04.m11: Salutations to you, the trainers of horses and the drivers of chariots.
m.namakam.a04.m12: Salutations to you, the carpenters and the chariot-makers.
m.namakam.a04.m13: Salutations to you, the potters and the smiths.
m.namakam.a04.m14: Salutations to you, the fowlers and the Niṣādas (forest-folk who fish and hunt).
m.namakam.a04.m15: Salutations to you, the makers of arrows and the makers of bows.
m.namakam.a04.m16: Salutations to you, the hunters and those who lead the hounds.
m.namakam.a04.m17: Salutations to you, the dogs and the masters of dogs.
m.namakam.a05.m01: Salutations to Bhava, from whom all beings arise, and to Rudra, who drives away sorrow.
m.namakam.a05.m02: Salutations to Śarva, the destroyer of sin, and to Paśupati, lord of all beings.
m.namakam.a05.m03: Salutations to the blue-throated one and to the one whose throat is also white.
m.namakam.a05.m04: Salutations to the one with matted locks and to the one with shaven head.
m.namakam.a05.m05: Salutations to the thousand-eyed one and to the one with a hundred bows.
m.namakam.a05.m06: Salutations to the dweller on the mountain and to Śipiviṣṭa, who pervades the rays of light.
m.namakam.a05.m07: Salutations to the most bountiful, who showers every wish, and to the bearer of arrows.
m.namakam.a05.m08: Salutations to the short one and to the dwarf.
m.namakam.a05.m09: Salutations to the vast one and to the most ancient.
m.namakam.a05.m10: Salutations to the ancient one and to the one who grows with praise.
m.namakam.a05.m11: Salutations to the foremost and to the first.
m.namakam.a05.m12: Salutations to the swift one and to the one who moves everywhere.
m.namakam.a05.m13: Salutations to him who is in the swift currents and in the flowing waters.
m.namakam.a05.m14: Salutations to him who is in the waves and in the still waters.
m.namakam.a05.m15: Salutations to him who is in the streams and on the islands.
m.namakam.a06.m01: Salutations to the eldest and to the youngest.
m.namakam.a06.m02: Salutations to the first-born and to the later-born.
m.namakam.a06.m03: Salutations to the middle-born and to the one not yet grown.
m.namakam.a06.m04: Salutations to him who is in the lowest and in the roots.
m.namakam.a06.m05: Salutations to him who is in the world of mixed deeds and in the protective charm.
m.namakam.a06.m06: Salutations to him who is in Yama’s realm and in the realm of well-being.
m.namakam.a06.m07: Salutations to him who is in the fertile fields and in the threshing-floors.
m.namakam.a06.m08: Salutations to him who is in the Vedic hymns and in the Upaniṣads, the end of the Veda.
m.namakam.a06.m09: Salutations to him who is in the forests and in the thickets.
m.namakam.a06.m10: Salutations to him who is the sound and its echo.
m.namakam.a06.m11: Salutations to him of the swift armies and of the swift chariots.
m.namakam.a06.m12: Salutations to the hero and to the one who breaks the foe apart.
m.namakam.a06.m13: Salutations to the armoured one and to the one with a sheltering chariot.
m.namakam.a06.m14: Salutations to the helmeted one and to the one with a breastplate.
m.namakam.a06.m15: Salutations to the renowned one and to him whose army is renowned.
m.namakam.a07.m01: Salutations to him who is in the drum and in the drumstick.
m.namakam.a07.m02: Salutations to the bold one and to the one who weighs up the foe.
m.namakam.a07.m03: Salutations to the messenger and to the one sent forth.
m.namakam.a07.m04: Salutations to him with sword and quiver.
m.namakam.a07.m05: Salutations to him of sharp arrows and to the armed one.
m.namakam.a07.m06: Salutations to him of fine weapons and of the good bow.
m.namakam.a07.m07: Salutations to him who is in the footpaths and on the roads.
m.namakam.a07.m08: Salutations to him who is in the rough channels and in the waters at the mountain’s foot.
m.namakam.a07.m09: Salutations to him who is in the marshes and in the lakes.
m.namakam.a07.m10: Salutations to him who is in the rivers and in the ponds.
m.namakam.a07.m11: Salutations to him who is in the wells and in the pits.
m.namakam.a07.m12: Salutations to him who is in the rain and in the drought.
m.namakam.a07.m13: Salutations to him who is in the clouds and in the lightning.
m.namakam.a07.m14: Salutations to him who is in the bright clouds and in the sunshine.
m.namakam.a07.m15: Salutations to him who is in the wind and in the storm.
m.namakam.a07.m16: Salutations to him who is in our dwellings and who guards them.
m.namakam.a08.m01: Salutations to Soma, who is ever with Umā, and to Rudra.
m.namakam.a08.m02: Salutations to the copper-red one and to the crimson one.
m.namakam.a08.m03: Salutations to him who brings happiness and to the lord of all beings.
m.namakam.a08.m04: Salutations to the fierce one and to the terrible one.
m.namakam.a08.m05: Salutations to him who slays in front and to him who slays from afar.
m.namakam.a08.m06: Salutations to the slayer and to the greatest slayer, who ends all at the dissolution.
m.namakam.a08.m07: Salutations to the trees with green leaves, his forms.
m.namakam.a08.m08: Salutations to Tāra, the deliverer who carries us across.
m.namakam.a08.m09: Salutations to Śambhu, the source of bliss, and to Mayobhu, the source of joy in this world.
m.namakam.a08.m10: Salutations to Śaṅkara, the giver of bliss, and to Mayaskara, the giver of joy.
m.namakam.a08.m11: Salutations to Śiva, the auspicious one, and to Śivatara, more auspicious than all.
m.namakam.a08.m12: Salutations to him who is in the holy fords and on the river banks.
m.namakam.a08.m13: Salutations to him who is on the far shore (liberation) and on the near shore (this world).
m.namakam.a08.m14: Salutations to him who helps us cross over and who brings us safely to the other shore.
m.namakam.a08.m15: Salutations to him who comes into this world to act, and who tastes the fruit of action.
m.namakam.a08.m16: Salutations to him who is in the tender grass and in the foam.
m.namakam.a08.m17: Salutations to him who is in the sands and in the flowing currents.
m.namakam.a09.m01: Salutations to him who is in the barren lands and on the broad highways.
m.namakam.a09.m02: Salutations to him who is in the gravelly places and in the dwellings.
m.namakam.a09.m03: Salutations to the matted-haired one and to him who stands before his devotees.
m.namakam.a09.m04: Salutations to him who is in the cow-pens and in the homes.
m.namakam.a09.m05: Salutations to him who is in the beds and in the mansions.
m.namakam.a09.m06: Salutations to him who is in the thorny thickets and in the caves.
m.namakam.a09.m07: Salutations to him who is in the deep pools and in the dew.
m.namakam.a09.m08: Salutations to him who is in the dust and in the fine powder.
m.namakam.a09.m09: Salutations to him who is in what is dry and in what is green.
m.namakam.a09.m10: Salutations to him who is in the bare ground and in the grass.
m.namakam.a09.m11: Salutations to him who is in the earth and in the fine waves.
m.namakam.a09.m12: Salutations to him who is in the leaves and in the falling of leaves.
m.namakam.a09.m13: Salutations to him who raises his weapon and to him who strikes.
m.namakam.a09.m14: Salutations to him who afflicts a little and to him who afflicts greatly.
m.namakam.a09.m15: Salutations to you who shower blessings, the hearts of the gods.
m.namakam.a09.m16: Salutations to those who destroy sins; salutations to those who discern good and evil.
m.namakam.a09.m17: Salutations to those who drive out sins; salutations to those who are present everywhere.
m.namakam.a10.m01: O you who make sinners flee, lord of the soma, owning nothing, blue and red one — do not frighten or harm these people or these cattle; let none of them fall sick.
m.namakam.a10.m02: O Rudra, your auspicious form is the healer every day; auspicious is Rudra’s medicine — with it, make us happy, that we may live.
m.namakam.a10.m03: To Rudra the mighty, the matted-haired, lord of heroes, we offer this prayer, that all be well with our two-footed and four-footed beings, and that all in this village be nourished and free from illness.
m.namakam.a10.m04: Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and give us joy; we serve you, lord of heroes, with salutations. The welfare and freedom from fear that father Manu won by worship — may we gain it under your guidance, O Rudra.
m.namakam.a10.m05: Do not harm our elders or our children, our young men or the child in the womb; do not slay our father or mother, nor harm our dear bodies, O Rudra.
m.namakam.a10.m06: Harm not our children and grandchildren, nor our life, our cows or our horses; O Rudra, in your anger do not slay our heroes. Bearing offerings, we serve you with salutations.
m.namakam.a10.m07: Far be from us your form that slays cattle and men; may your favour be with us, lord of heroes. Protect us, speak for us, O god, and grant us shelter, you who are mighty in both worlds.
m.namakam.a10.m08: Praise the renowned youth who dwells in the heart’s cave, fearsome like a lion and mighty to destroy. Praised by us, O Rudra, be gracious to your singer; let your armies strike others, not us.
m.namakam.a10.m09: May Rudra’s weapon pass us by, and the ill will of the fierce one who seeks to harm; slacken your strong bow for your generous worshippers, O bountiful one, and be gracious to our children and grandchildren.
m.namakam.a10.m10: Most bountiful, most auspicious one, be gracious and kind to us. Laying down your weapon on the highest tree, wearing the elephant hide, come to us holding only the Pināka bow.
m.namakam.a10.m11: O scatterer of sorrows, red-hued one, salutations to you, O Lord. May your thousand weapons strike others, away from us.
m.namakam.a10.m12: Thousands upon thousands are the weapons in your arms; O Lord, you who are their master, turn their points away from us.
m.namakam.a11.m01: The thousands upon thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth — we unstring their bows and lay them a thousand yojanas away.
m.namakam.a11.m02: The Bhavas who dwell in this great ocean of the sky; the blue-throated, white-throated Śarvas who roam the earth below —
m.namakam.a11.m03: the blue-throated, white-throated Rudras who have reached heaven; those in the trees, tawny like young grass, blue-throated and red —
m.namakam.a11.m04: those who are the lords of beings, with shaven heads and with matted hair —
m.namakam.a11.m05: those who afflict people in their food, and those who drink from their vessels —
m.namakam.a11.m06: those who guard the paths, who bring sustenance and fight for it —
m.namakam.a11.m07: those who roam the holy places, armed with spears and swords —
m.namakam.a11.m08: and the Rudras, as many as these and more, who have spread through the directions —
m.namakam.a11.m09: we unstring their bows and lay them a thousand yojanas away.
m.namakam.a11.m10: Salutations to the Rudras who are on earth, in the sky and in heaven, whose arrows are food, wind and rain. To them, ten (fingers joined) to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, ten upward — salutations. May they make us happy. The one we hate and the one who hates us, we place in your jaws.
m.namakam.uttara.u1: We worship the three-eyed Lord, fragrant, who increases nourishment. As the ripe cucumber is freed from its stalk, may I be freed from death, but not from immortality.
m.namakam.uttara.u2: The Rudra who is in fire, who is in the waters, who has entered the plants, the Rudra who has entered all the worlds — to that Rudra, salutations.
m.namakam.uttara.u3: Praise him who has good arrows and a good bow, who rules over every remedy.
m.namakam.uttara.u4: We worship Rudra for a gracious mind; with salutations, serve the god who gives life.
m.namakam.uttara.u5: This hand of mine is blessed, this hand of mine more blessed still; this hand of mine heals all, its touch is auspicious.
m.namakam.uttara.u6: O Death, the thousand and ten thousand nooses you hold to slay mortals — all of them we remove by the power of the sacrifice.
m.namakam.uttara.u7: Svāhā to Death, svāhā to Death — this offering is to Death.
m.namakam.uttara.u8: You are the knot that holds the life-breaths; O Rudra, ender of all, enter me. Be nourished by this food. Salutations to Rudra who is Viṣṇu; protect me from death.
m.namakam.uttara.shanti: Sadāśiva, Om. Om, peace, peace, peace.
m.chamakam.a01.m01: Om. O Agni and Viṣṇu, rejoicing together, may these praises make you grow strong; come to us with splendour and with plenty.
m.chamakam.a01.m02: May I have food and the power to enjoy it.
m.chamakam.a01.m03: May I have the effort to begin and the drive to carry it through.
m.chamakam.a01.m04: May I have good thoughts and the will to act on them.
m.chamakam.a01.m05: May I have a fine voice and good fame.
m.chamakam.a01.m06: May I have the gift of being heard and the gift of hearing (the Veda).
m.chamakam.a01.m07: May I have light (insight) and heaven.
m.chamakam.a01.m08: May I have prāṇa, the breath that moves upward, and apāna, the breath that moves downward.
m.chamakam.a01.m09: May I have vyāna, the breath that pervades the body, and life itself.
m.chamakam.a01.m10: May I have a thinking mind and the knowledge it gathers.
m.chamakam.a01.m11: May I have speech and mind.
m.chamakam.a01.m12: May I have sight and hearing.
m.chamakam.a01.m13: May I have skill and strength.
m.chamakam.a01.m14: May I have vigour and the power to endure.
m.chamakam.a01.m15: May I have long life and a ripe old age.
m.chamakam.a01.m16: May I have a sound self and a sound body.
m.chamakam.a01.m17: May I have shelter and armour, sound limbs and sound bones.
m.chamakam.a01.m18: May I have sound joints and a sound body in every part.
m.chamakam.a02.m01: May I have pre-eminence and lordship.
m.chamakam.a02.m02: May I have righteous anger and its fire, steadiness, and the depth of waters.
m.chamakam.a02.m03: May I have victory and greatness.
m.chamakam.a02.m04: May I have breadth and abundance.
m.chamakam.a02.m05: May I have stature and a long line of descendants.
m.chamakam.a02.m06: May I have plenty and its growth.
m.chamakam.a02.m07: May I have truth and faith.
m.chamakam.a02.m08: May I have moving wealth (cattle) and riches.
m.chamakam.a02.m09: May I have self-mastery and radiance.
m.chamakam.a02.m10: May I have play and delight.
m.chamakam.a02.m11: May I have children born and children yet to be born.
m.chamakam.a02.m12: May I have sacred hymns and good deeds.
m.chamakam.a02.m13: May I have wealth gained and wealth still to be gained.
m.chamakam.a02.m14: May I have a good past and a good future.
m.chamakam.a02.m15: May I have easy ways and good paths.
m.chamakam.a02.m16: May I have prosperity and its increase.
m.chamakam.a02.m17: May I have what is fitting, and the power to make things fit.
m.chamakam.a02.m18: May I have understanding and right judgement.
m.chamakam.a03.m01: May I have happiness here and happiness hereafter.
m.chamakam.a03.m02: May I have what is dear, the desire for it, and its fulfilment.
m.chamakam.a03.m03: May I have a cheerful mind and good fortune.
m.chamakam.a03.m04: May I have the highest good and a good home.
m.chamakam.a03.m05: May I have fame, good fortune and wealth.
m.chamakam.a03.m06: May I have a guide (a teacher) and a supporter (a protector).
m.chamakam.a03.m07: May I have security and steadfastness.
m.chamakam.a03.m08: May I have the goodwill of all and honour.
m.chamakam.a03.m09: May I have knowledge of the Veda and the power to make it known.
m.chamakam.a03.m10: May I have the power to lead others and to bring forth children.
m.chamakam.a03.m11: May I have the plough (good farming) and freedom from obstacles in it.
m.chamakam.a03.m12: May I have the fruit of right action and of heaven, freedom from disease and from illness.
m.chamakam.a03.m13: May I have the means of life, long life, freedom from enemies and freedom from fear.
m.chamakam.a03.m14: May I have a good way of living and good rest.
m.chamakam.a03.m15: May I have a good dawn and good days.
m.chamakam.a04.m01: May I have food and pleasant, truthful speech.
m.chamakam.a04.m02: May I have milk and its essence.
m.chamakam.a04.m03: May I have ghee and honey.
m.chamakam.a04.m04: May I eat and drink in the company of others.
m.chamakam.a04.m05: May I have good farming and good rain.
m.chamakam.a04.m06: May I have fertile land and growing plants.
m.chamakam.a04.m07: May I have gold and precious things.
m.chamakam.a04.m08: May I have plenty and its nourishing power.
m.chamakam.a04.m09: May I have abundance and mastery.
m.chamakam.a04.m10: May I have much, and more and more.
m.chamakam.a04.m11: May I have fullness and greater fullness, what never runs out, good grain, food, and freedom from hunger.
m.chamakam.a04.m12: May I have rice and barley.
m.chamakam.a04.m13: May I have black gram and sesame.
m.chamakam.a04.m14: May I have green gram and chickpeas.
m.chamakam.a04.m15: May I have wheat and lentils.
m.chamakam.a04.m16: May I have millet and fine grains.
m.chamakam.a04.m17: May I have śyāmāka millet and wild rice.
m.chamakam.a05.m01: May I have stone and clay.
m.chamakam.a05.m02: May I have hills and mountains.
m.chamakam.a05.m03: May I have sand and great trees.
m.chamakam.a05.m04: May I have gold and iron.
m.chamakam.a05.m05: May I have lead and tin.
m.chamakam.a05.m06: May I have copper and bronze, and fire.
m.chamakam.a05.m07: May I have water, creepers and healing herbs.
m.chamakam.a05.m08: May I have crops from tilled land and crops that grow wild.
m.chamakam.a05.m09: May I have domestic animals and wild ones — may all these be secured for me through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a05.m10: May I have inherited wealth and the power to gain more.
m.chamakam.a05.m11: May I have prosperity and its glory.
m.chamakam.a05.m12: May I have riches and a dwelling.
m.chamakam.a05.m13: May I have worthy work, the power to do it, and its purpose achieved.
m.chamakam.a05.m14: May I have my aims, the means to reach them, and arrival.
m.chamakam.a06.m01: May Agni, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m02: May Soma, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m03: May Savitṛ, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m04: May Sarasvatī, and Indra with her, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m05: May Pūṣan, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m06: May Bṛhaspati, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m07: May Mitra, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m08: May Varuṇa, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m09: May Tvaṣṭṛ, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m10: May Dhātṛ, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m11: May Viṣṇu, and Indra with him, be mine; may the Aśvins, and Indra with them, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m12: May the Maruts, and Indra with them, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m13: May the Viśvedevas, and Indra with them, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m14: May the earth, and Indra with it, be mine; may the sky between, and Indra with it, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m15: May heaven, and Indra with it, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m16: May the directions, and Indra with them, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m17: May the zenith, and Indra with it, be mine.
m.chamakam.a06.m18: May Prajāpati, and Indra with him, be mine.
m.chamakam.a07.m01: May I have the cups of soma: the aṃśu and the raśmi, the adābhya and the adhipati.
m.chamakam.a07.m02: May I have the upāṃśu and the antaryāma cups.
m.chamakam.a07.m03: May I have the cups for Indra and Vāyu, and for Mitra and Varuṇa.
m.chamakam.a07.m04: May I have the cup for the Aśvins and the pratiprasthāna.
m.chamakam.a07.m05: May I have the śukra and the manthin cups.
m.chamakam.a07.m06: May I have the āgrayaṇa and the vaiśvadeva cups.
m.chamakam.a07.m07: May I have the dhruva and the vaiśvānara cups.
m.chamakam.a07.m08: May I have the cups of the seasons and the atigrāhya cups.
m.chamakam.a07.m09: May I have the cups for Indra and Agni, and for the Viśvedevas.
m.chamakam.a07.m10: May I have the marutvatīya cups and the cup for great Indra.
m.chamakam.a07.m11: May I have the cups for Āditya and for Savitṛ.
m.chamakam.a07.m12: May I have the cups for Sarasvatī and for Pūṣan.
m.chamakam.a07.m13: May I have the pātnīvata cup and the hāriyojana cup.
m.chamakam.a08.m01: May I have the sacred firewood and the kuśa grass.
m.chamakam.a08.m02: May I have the altar and the side-altars.
m.chamakam.a08.m03: May I have the ladles and the soma-cups.
m.chamakam.a08.m04: May I have the pressing-stones and the svarus (chips cut from the sacrificial post).
m.chamakam.a08.m05: May I have the sounding-holes and the pressing-boards.
m.chamakam.a08.m06: May I have the droṇa-kalaśa and the vessels for Vāyu.
m.chamakam.a08.m07: May I have the vessel for purified soma and the vessel for stirring it.
m.chamakam.a08.m08: May I have the āgnīdhra fire-place and the shed for offerings.
m.chamakam.a08.m09: May I have the sacrificial halls, the seat-shed, and the rice-cakes offered.
m.chamakam.a08.m10: May I have the cooked offerings, the closing bath, and the svagākāra rite.
m.chamakam.a09.m01: May I have the fire, the gharma rite and the arka.
m.chamakam.a09.m02: May I have the sun, the life-breath and the horse sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a09.m03: May I have the earth, Aditi and Diti.
m.chamakam.a09.m04: May I have heaven, the śakvarī verses, the fingers, and the directions.
m.chamakam.a09.m05: May these be secured through the sacrifice. May I have the Ṛk (hymns).
m.chamakam.a09.m06: May I have the Sāman (chants) and the stoma (hymn-sequences).
m.chamakam.a09.m07: May I have the Yajus (formulas) and consecration (dīkṣā).
m.chamakam.a09.m08: May I have austerity and the seasons.
m.chamakam.a09.m09: May I have the vow, day and night, rain, and the bṛhat and rathantara chants —
m.chamakam.a09.m10: may these two be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m01: May I have cattle yet in the womb and calves.
m.chamakam.a10.m02: May I have a bull and a cow of a year and a half.
m.chamakam.a10.m03: May I have a bull and a cow of two years.
m.chamakam.a10.m04: May I have a bull and a cow of two and a half years.
m.chamakam.a10.m05: May I have a bull and a cow of three years.
m.chamakam.a10.m06: May I have a bull and a cow of three and a half years.
m.chamakam.a10.m07: May I have a bull and a cow of four years.
m.chamakam.a10.m08: May I have a strong bull and a barren cow.
m.chamakam.a10.m09: May I have a mature bull, a cow that has miscarried, and an ox for the cart.
m.chamakam.a10.m10: May I have a milch cow. May life be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m11: May prāṇa be secured through the sacrifice; may apāna be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m12: May vyāna be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m13: May sight be secured through the sacrifice; may hearing be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m14: May the mind be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m15: May speech be secured through the sacrifice; may the self be secured through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a10.m16: May the sacrifice itself be fulfilled through the sacrifice.
m.chamakam.a11.m01: May one and three be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m02: May five and seven be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m03: May nine and eleven be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m04: May thirteen and fifteen be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m05: May seventeen and nineteen be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m06: May twenty-one and twenty-three be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m07: May twenty-five and twenty-seven be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m08: May twenty-nine and thirty-one be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m09: May thirty-three be mine; may four and eight be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m10: May twelve and sixteen be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m11: May twenty, twenty-four and twenty-eight be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m12: May thirty-two and thirty-six be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m13: May forty, forty-four and forty-eight be mine.
m.chamakam.a11.m14: May food, its bringing forth, and its growth be mine;
m.chamakam.a11.m15: the will to act, heaven, and the highest place;
m.chamakam.a11.m16: the all-pervading one, the one at the end, and the final one;
m.chamakam.a11.m17: the one born of the world, the world itself, and its sovereign lord.
m.chamakam.shanti.shanti: Om. Iḍā guides the offering to the gods, Manu leads the sacrifice, Bṛhaspati recites the hymns of praise; the Viśvedevas speak the sacred verses. O mother Earth, do not harm me. May I think sweetly, act sweetly, offer sweetly, speak sweetly. May I speak to the gods sweet words, worth hearing for men. May the gods guard me for my good, and the ancestors rejoice. Om, peace, peace, peace.

namakam.purva.guru: “Hariḥ Om” is the customary opening of Vedic recitation.
namakam.purva.ganapati: In the Ṛgveda (2.23.1) this ṛk is addressed to Brahmaṇaspati, lord of prayer; tradition recites it to Śrī Gaṇeśa before any undertaking, so that it goes without obstacles.
namakam.purva.samhita: The Namakam is Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5 and the Chamakam 4.7. Both are recited in the Śatarudrīya rite, offerings to the hundred forms of Rudra in the building of the great fire-altar (agnicayana).
namakam.a01.m01: Rudra’s wrath falls on wrongdoing. The first anuvāka bows to his anger and weapons so that they become gracious toward the worshipper; this is why the Rudram is recited for peace (śānti).
namakam.a01.m03: Giriśanta: “who, dwelling on the mountain (Kailāsa), spreads happiness (śam).”
namakam.a01.m06: Rudra is praised as the physician (bhiṣak) of body and of saṃsāra; “serpents” and “yātudhānīs” stand for every hidden harm.
namakam.a01.m07: Sāyaṇa: here Rudra is seen in the Sun, whose colour changes through the morning; the Sun’s rays are the many Rudras.
namakam.a01.m08: Nīlagrīva, “blue-throated”: in the Purāṇas Śiva’s throat turned blue when he held the hālāhala poison from the churning of the ocean to save the worlds.
namakam.bhagavan.namaste: This hymn of names is recited after the first anuvāka by tradition; it is not part of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.
namakam.a02.m01: From the second anuvāka on, Rudra is saluted as present in, and lord of, everything: the trees, the paths, the fields, the herbs. Each mantra ends with “namaḥ” (namo), which joins it to the next.
namakam.a02.m02: Paśu, “the bound one”, is every embodied soul bound by the noose (pāśa) of ignorance; Paśupati is the lord who sets it free.
namakam.a03.m01: Here Rudra is saluted even as the lord of thieves and robbers. The commentators explain that nothing exists apart from him; in his play (līlā) he is the inner controller of every being, so even these are his forms.
namakam.a03.m09: “Vaḥ”, to you (plural): from here the Rudras in their many forms are addressed.
namakam.a04.m01: The feminine forms here are read as Rudra’s śaktis, the divine mothers (Brāhmī and the others) who attend him.
namakam.a05.m01: Rudra: “he who drives away sorrow (rut)”, as the commentators explain the name. The fifth anuvāka salutes Rudra’s own forms and names.
namakam.a05.m06: Śipiviṣṭa is also a name of Viṣṇu; tradition sees in it the oneness of Hari and Hara.
namakam.a08.m01: Soma is read as sa-Umā, “he who is with Umā (Pārvatī)”.
namakam.a08.m08: Tāra, “who carries across” the ocean of saṃsāra, is also a name of the praṇava, Om.
namakam.a08.m11: “Namaḥ śivāya”: the five-syllable Pañcākṣarī mantra stands here, in the eighth of the eleven anuvākas, at the heart of the Rudram. Śaiva tradition calls the Rudram the heart of the Vedas and this mantra its life.
namakam.a09.m15: The last three mantras address the Rudras who dwell in the hearts of the gods: Agni, Vāyu and Āditya, as Sāyaṇa explains.
namakam.a10.m01: The tenth anuvāka is a prayer for protection of family, cattle and life, and for Rudra’s healing form.
namakam.a10.m10: Kṛtti is the hide Śiva wears (the elephant- or tiger-skin of the Purāṇas); Pināka is his bow. He comes carrying it only as an ornament, not to strike.
namakam.a11.m01: In the eleventh anuvāka the Rudras of every region are named, and the refrain “tanmasi” asks that their bows be unstrung and laid far away. A yojana is a measure of distance.
namakam.a11.m10: “Ten” is read as the ten fingers joined in añjali. The last sentence is commonly understood as handing over all enmity, ours and others’, to Rudra to be destroyed.
namakam.uttara.u1: The Mahāmṛtyuñjaya mantra (Ṛgveda 7.59.12; TS 1.8.6). The mantras from here to the end are recited after the eleventh anuvāka by tradition; they are not part of TS 4.5.
namakam.uttara.u5: Said while touching the Śiva-liṅga or one’s own body: the hand that has worshipped Rudra becomes a healing hand.
namakam.uttara.u8: “Rudrāya viṣṇave”: Rudra and Viṣṇu are saluted as one.
namakam.uttara.shanti: Peace is asked three times: from troubles within (ādhyātmika), from other beings (ādhibhautika) and from the forces of nature and fate (ādhidaivika).
chamakam.a01.m01: In the Chamakam the worshipper asks, through the yajña, for every good thing in life. Each line says “… ca me”, “and (may) … (be) mine”, and is completed by “yajñena kalpantām”, “may they be secured through the sacrifice”, spoken at the end of several anuvākas. Offered with Agni and Viṣṇu, the prayer becomes worship: the gifts asked for are received as Rudra’s grace.
chamakam.a02.m01: The second anuvāka asks for standing, character and every kind of growth.
chamakam.a03.m01: The third anuvāka asks for happiness, well-being and protection in this life and beyond.
chamakam.a04.m01: The fourth anuvāka asks for food, crops and plenty; it names the grains of the Vedic household.
chamakam.a05.m01: The fifth anuvāka asks for the earth’s resources: stones, metals, waters, plants and animals.
chamakam.a06.m01: The sixth anuvāka names the gods, each paired with Indra, to whom shares of the offering go (the ardhendra offerings): may each of them, with Indra, be favourable to me.
chamakam.a07.m01: The seventh anuvāka names the grahas, the cups or draughts of soma drawn for each deity in the soma sacrifice. To ask for them is to ask for the whole rite and its fruit.
chamakam.a08.m01: The eighth anuvāka names what the sacrifice needs: fuel, altars, ladles, pressing-stones, vessels, sheds and the closing rites.
chamakam.a09.m01: The ninth anuvāka asks for the great rites and the powers that sustain them: the sun, the earth, the Vedas, consecration and austerity.
chamakam.a10.m01: The tenth anuvāka names cattle by age (a year and a half, two, two and a half, three, three and a half, four years), then offers life, the senses and the sacrifice itself back to the sacrifice.
chamakam.a11.m01: The eleventh anuvāka counts the odd numbers from one to thirty-three and the multiples of four from four to forty-eight. Sāyaṇa reads them as the measures of verses and rites; others see in the odd numbers the thirty-three gods and in the fours the Vedas. The last lines name the powers that rule time and the worlds.
chamakam.a11.m17: These twelve names (vāja, prasava, apija, kratu, suvaḥ, mūrdhā, vyaśniya, āntyāyana, antya, bhauvana, bhuvana, adhipati) are read as the presiding powers of the twelve months, or of the stages of creation.
chamakam.shanti.shanti: This śānti mantra closes the Chamakam; the prayer for sweetness of thought, deed and speech sums up the Rudram.
